```{r load-lib, include = FALSE}
library(tidyverse)
library(readr)
library(janitor)
library(ggplot2)
library(scales)
```


```{r load-data, include=TRUE}
# load data 
seoul_bikes_raw <- read_csv("data/SeoulBikeData.csv", locale=locale(encoding="latin1"))
#extracting raw data, locale needed to be specified as error otherwise.

#clean data
seoul_bikes <- seoul_bikes_raw |> 
  clean_names()
#cleaning names to snake_case, as column headings' words initially separated with space

#looking above at the variable table, it might mean that on non-functional days, there will be no bikes rented whatsoever. We can run the following code to verify:
seoul_bikes |>
  filter(functioning_day == "No" & rented_bike_count > 0)

seoul_bikes <- seoul_bikes |> 
  filter(functioning_day != "No") |>  
  subset(select = -functioning_day)
#after dropping non-functioning days, we can drop the functioning_day variable entirely, as it has become redundant.
```


## Research Question

**How resilient is the demand for rented bikes to adverse weather conditions across different functional time windows (e.g. peak commuting hours vs. weekend leisure hours)?**
